headline: iOS 27 revamps Shortcuts app with AI-powered 'Describe a Short' feature
summary: iOS 27 integrates Apple Intelligence into Shortcuts, allowing users to create automations conversationally. This makes complex scripting accessible, transforming the app into an essential tool for daily tasks.
details: Apple's Shortcuts app in iOS 27 is getting a major overhaul, making automation accessible even for first-time users. The new 'Describe a Short' feature, powered by Apple Intelligence, allows users to create complex workflows using natural language.

Users can simply tell the app what they want to automate, and it generates the flow. While still in beta, this conversational approach significantly lowers the barrier to entry, making scripting optional for power users.

One practical example is a shortcut that prompts users when opening social media apps like Instagram, asking if they truly want to use it. Choosing 'no' automatically closes the app and locks the screen, helping to break mindless scrolling habits.

Another useful automation checks local air quality every morning and sends a notification if it exceeds a set threshold. This eliminates the need for manual checks, ensuring users are informed about environmental conditions before leaving home.

Location-based shortcuts can also be created, such as one that reminds users to bring a power bank if their iPhone battery is below 50% when leaving home. This proactive alert helps avoid being stranded with a dead phone.

For home management, a two-part shortcut logs plant watering times with a tap on a home screen icon. A second automation then checks if plants have been watered within the last week, sending a reminder if not.

Finally, a screenshot automation automatically extracts and copies text from any new screenshot to the clipboard. This streamlines the process of capturing and using text from images, saving multiple manual steps.

headline: 14-year-old ships 3 projects using only a Samsung M11 and free mobile code editors
summary: A 14-year-old developer is building and shipping web and C/C++ projects entirely from a Samsung M11 smartphone, utilizing free mobile code editors like TrebEdit and Cxxdroid. This setup has already yielded three completed projects, including a portfolio and co
details: A 14-year-old developer, Adrish Datta, has successfully shipped three coding projects using only a Samsung M11 smartphone. Lacking a traditional PC or laptop, Adrish relies on free mobile code editors like TrebEdit for web development and Cxxdroid for C/C++ programming.

Adrish's portfolio showcases his work, including a calculator and a password generator. The calculator and password generator were collaborative efforts, with Adrish handling HTML/CSS and a friend contributing JavaScript.

Adrish is actively seeking feedback on his code, feature suggestions, and ideas for future projects to further enhance his skills. This approach highlights a proactive and community-driven learning style.
